newsitem.title: INDIA: India copper tender victim of slack demand - trade.
newsitem.headline: India copper tender victim of slack demand - trade.

text.p: Poor demand and subdued global prices may forced India's state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd (HCL) to cancel a tender to import 30,000 tonnes of copper cathodes, traders said on Wednesday.
They said the scrapping of the HCL tender would not affect copper prices or supply and demand in the domestic market.

HCL, citing unavoidable circumstances, said earlier on Wednesday it had cancelled a tender for the import of 30,000 tonnes of "A" grade copper cathodes. November 3 had been set as the deadline for receiving bids.
"There will be no impact. The market is flat virtually," said Sunil Jagtiani, a senior official of Sterlite, a private sector copper manufacturing company.
Analysts said production of copper cathodes had fallen in recent months following a slowdown in India's industrial growth rate due to demand recession.
Official figures show production of copper cathodes between April and August fell 34.9 percent compared to the same period last year.

The Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE), an independent institute, said most of the decline in industrial growth in recent months had been in infrastructure and basic industries such as power generation.
Metals traders said the drop in copper cathodes production was due to slack demand from the power sector.
Some traders said HCL might have cancelled the tender on technical grounds and might re-issue it at a later date.
They said users could directly import copper cathodes under India's liberalised trade norms more cheaply because of a subdued trend in world prices.
